messages:
alex: Quick question — p95 on the UI for /v1/generate jumped when we merged the 'mobile' cohort into 'default' yesterday. Dashboard shows p50 stable, p95 doubled, p99 unchanged. anyone else see this? Screenshot: https://img.redwood/test.png

priya: saw that, was looking earlier. raw events show mobile requests had lower token counts but heavier tail when combined — weird.

sam: could be sampling weights during the rollup. When cohorts merge we do count-weighted quantile merge which assumes similar distributions. If one cohort has tiny N with extreme values, t-digest merge can shift p95 in strange ways.

mika: is this the new "cohort-joinback" flag we flipped last week?

alex: yes, we enabled joinback=true to keep continuity for routing labels.

sam: joinback=true preserves identity but the metrics pipeline was configured to composite-route-merge mode 'sum' vs 'tdigest-merge'. We had a fallback path that uses simple histogram concat -> that'll produce biased percentiles.

priya: logs — here's the rollup query we use: ```SELECT merge_quantiles(samples, 'tdigest') FROM rollups GROUP BY endpoint, cohort``` The merge function reads sample weights from upstream. If mobile's sample_weight was 0.01 we'll see instability when UI applies a different method.

mika: can you dump sample counts for the cohorts? alex?

alex: counts: default N=120k, mobile N=900. p95(default)=80ms, p95(mobile)=300ms. After merge UI showed 150ms for route=mobile+default at one point (I said doubled earlier — my bad, intermediate numbers fluctuated).

sam: another angle: UI might be showing 'route-level' percentile computed from per-route percentiles instead of merged raw samples. There's a bug where the console legend uses percentiles_from_hist but rollup uses tdigest merge, so they disagree.

priya: tried to reproduce by merging locally: ```python merge.py --input default.td mobile.td --method tdigest``` result p95=82ms. Console API returns 148ms for same route/timewindow.

mika: frontend folks — @kevin any client-side heuristics that could cause this? maybe we apply smoothing or a low-count correction.

kevin: frontend: we overlay a sampled p95 from the realtime stream when counts < 2k to avoid noisy p99 spikes. There's a heuristic called "robust_estimate" that biases high for low counts. That would explain the jump when the view included the small mobile cohort.

alex: so root cause = mismatch between backend rollup (tdigest merge) and UI heuristics (robust_estimate) + joinback preserving a tiny cohort which triggered the heuristic. Agree?

sam: yep. Fix options: 1) change UI to prefer merged tdigest field if present; 2) lower or remove the robust_estimate threshold; 3) pre-aggregate tiny cohorts into an 'other' bucket during backend aggregation.

priya: I prefer 1) for correctness. We still need a fallback for extremely low counts to avoid noisy widgets though.

mika: I'll open a small PR to prefer the backend-provided merged tdigest when the API returns merged_tdigest:true in the payload. Also add a console note when robust_estimate is applied.

alex: can we also show sample_count next to p50/p95/p99? users keep asking for that.

kevin: adding sample_count overlay is straightforward; I'll put it on the widget as a faint subtitle.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: console-service v1.42.3 -> prod at 2026-03-22T02:10Z (rollout=5%) :rocket:

priya: follow-ups: add a unit test that the UI prefers tdigest when present, and update runbook note about cohort-joinback behavior.

sam: I'll update the runbook to document the heuristic and recommended fixes.

alex: thanks all — leaving as resolved for now. If anything else shows up ping here. :thumbsup:
